lateral-flow.name: Colloidal Gold Lateral Flow Immunoassay
lateral-flow.what: Lateral flow immunoassay (LFIA) is the technology behind rapid diagnostic tests — a paper-based strip that detects a target analyte via labeled antibodies and capillary flow, producing a visible line within minutes.
lateral-flow.how: A sample is applied to the sample pad and migrates by capillary action through the conjugate pad (where colloidal-gold–labeled antibodies bind the analyte), along the nitrocellulose membrane (where the test and control lines are immobilized), and into the absorbent pad. A visible test line forms when the labeled complex is captured.
lateral-flow.why_matters: It is instrument-free, room-temperature-stable and read by eye — the basis for point-of-care screening across infectious disease, cardiac markers and drug testing. Understanding the components is how buyers evaluate batch consistency and cut-off reliability.
components: Sample pad — receives and pre-treats the sample
Nitrocellulose membrane — test and control lines

conjugation.name: Colloidal Gold Conjugation
conjugation.what: Conjugation is the process of attaching detection antibodies to colloidal gold nanoparticles (typically ~40 nm), producing the colored label that makes the test line visible.
conjugation.how: Gold nanoparticles are synthesized and then passively adsorb antibodies via electrostatic and hydrophobic interaction; the conjugate is stabilized, blocked and dispensed onto the conjugate pad. Batch-to-batch control of particle size and antibody density determines signal intensity and consistency.
conjugation.why_matters: Conjugate quality directly affects sensitivity and the clarity of the result line — a key QC point and a common source of batch variation that buyers should ask about.

membrane.name: Nitrocellulose Membrane & Test Lines
membrane.what: The nitrocellulose membrane is where the test and control lines are immobilized — the readout zone of a lateral-flow test.
membrane.how: A capture antibody is dispensed at the test line and an anti-species (control) antibody at the control line. As the sample–conjugate complex flows past, it binds at the test line (proportional to analyte) and always binds at the control line (confirming the test ran correctly).
membrane.why_matters: The control line validates each device, and test-line intensity reflects analyte level — understanding this is key to reading results and spotting invalid tests.
components: Membrane pore size — controls flow rate and line sharpness

fia.name: Fluorescence Immunoassay (FIA)
fia.what: Fluorescence immunoassay uses a fluorescent label instead of colloidal gold and is read by a dedicated analyzer, producing quantitative (not just qualitative) results.
fia.how: A fluorescent conjugate binds the analyte and is captured at the test line; a fluorescence analyzer measures the emitted signal intensity, which is converted to a concentration via a calibration curve.
fia.why_matters: FIA upgrades rapid tests from qualitative triage to quantitative measurement — relevant for cardiac markers, hormones and inflammation markers where a numeric result adds clinical value.
